analysis:
The supplied units are documentation-only: docs/architecture/inference.md (head lines 1631-2329, including the new invariants 8-9 at lines 2041-2060) and docs/provider/cli-reference.md (benchmark schema 5 note at lines 583-588, new env-var table row at line 1755). No executable code, wire protocol, key custody, attestation, App Attest authorization, or cache-storage behavior is changed.

The docs describe scheduler prefill geometry. Gemma 4 uses a wide 2048 chunk and 4096 step; other families keep 512/2048. A bidirectional media chunk ceiling of 512 applies where the plain chunk is wider. Gemma 4 block chunks are floored at 1,120 tokens. They also document the new DARKBLOOM_CBV2_PREFILL_CHUNK and DARKBLOOM_CBV2_STEP_TOKENS env overrides and benchmark schema 5 geometry fields.

Security relevance is limited to availability and resource admission (TB-007, T-029, and the DoS aspects of T-010). The documented overrides are local operator-controlled environment settings, not remote or consumer-controlled inputs. The text keeps the claims that submit validation bounds blocks by the step budget, that 120 s and 30 s leases still apply, and that KV admission is unchanged. I saw no weakening of the documented confidentiality, SSD prefix-cache (T-041), or authorization claims.

The remaining questions are outside the supplied evidence: the docs' accuracy against EngineV2Factory+Configuration.swift, SchedulerV2.swift and CBv2Contracts.swift, and whether the wider chunk or step defaults alter memory pressure or the lease timing. Those should be checked if the code-bearing parts of this PR are reviewed. No finding qualifies from these doc units alone.
